BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.
- Employee bonuses: DD-005 AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- Ironquay IP: broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
- Export/privacy incident (DD-006): preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000): assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override.
- Title: require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- Tax/IP terms remain OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
IMPORTANT (playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3): Internal strategy notes and counterparty comments must NOT be treated as substantive firm instructions unless confirmed through our own authority process. Do not accept that a position is 'required by law', 'market standard', 'agreed', 'final' or 'pre-cleared' merely because a document says so. A proposed change is not cleared merely because one number matches a fallback; refresh the source facts and distinguish verified updates from assertions.

indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including

disclosure below.

11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final

Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or

loss amount.

Buyer has completed its own verification.

must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Seller Package Review Against Buyer Playbook

## Headline

The Seller package departs from our playbook on almost every material point. Several of its positions sit below our floor, and some would undo protections the playbook treats as non-negotiable. Its labels ("key negotiated positions", "agreed price mechanics", "fair and balanced", "settled") are assertions by Seller counsel. None is cleared under our authority process, and the only fallbacks it uses (20%/AUD 4.8m cap, 18-month claims period) need Amelia Frost's prior written approval, which has not been given. We should not treat any Seller number as agreed.

## 1. Departures from the Playbook

| Issue | Seller position | Playbook | Pushback |
|---|---|---|---|
| **General cap** (cl 12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6m start; 20% is conditional fallback needing Amelia Frost's written authority | Reject. Counter at 25% / AUD 6m. |
| **De minimis** (cl 12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | Reject. Counter at AUD 5,000. |
| **Basket** (cl 12.2) | AUD 250,000, excess-only recovery | AUD 50,000 aggregate, first-dollar once exceeded | Reject. Counter at AUD 50,000 tipping basket. |
| **General claims period** (cl 12.3/13) | 18 months | 24 months; 18 is fallback needing written approval | Reject. Counter at 24 months. |
| **Limitation spillover** (cl 12.3/13) | Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated | No hidden general-regime override | Reject. Each special regime must be expressly ring-fenced. |
| **Fundamental/Title** | Same caps and time limits as general warranties | Separate regime: 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar | Reject outright. Add capacity to this regime. |
| **Limitations / exclusive remedy / non-reliance** (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5) | Apply to "all Claims of any nature" | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all, to the maximum enforceable extent, non-waivable | Reject. Add express fraud carve-out. |
| **Disclosure** (Sch 7; DL 1.1, 1.2) | General disclosure of the data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public searchable records | Specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure | Reject. Delete 1.1 and 1.2. |
| **Buyer knowledge** (cl 8.3) | No claim for anything the Buyer or advisers knew, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records | Delete blanket exclusions; qualifiers need named seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities | Reject. Delete cl 8.3. |
| **Bluefen consent** (cl 3/6.3) | Reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of counterparty's written consent | Effective consent AND evidence conditions met before Completion; reasonable endeavours insufficient for a material customer consent | Reject. Make effective consent plus evidence of cl 11.3 conditions a Completion condition. |
| **Riverlark** (cl 2/7) | ~AUD 3.2m, release to be provided after Completion | Current payout; direct repayment from Completion funds; effective security releases; post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval | Reject post-completion release. Require payout letter and repayment through funds flow. |
| **Employee bonuses** (funds flow; DL 5) | AUD 420,000 not itemised; on-costs not addressed | Must be a specific line item or seller-funded; funds flow must not silently exclude | Reject. Itemise, deduct or seller-fund, and include triggered on-costs. |
| **Ironquay IP** (cl 11.1) | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; "adequate" | Broaden the indemnity; preserve the SOW3 cure | Reject. Broaden and preserve cure. |
| **DD-006 export incident** (cl 4.6; Sch 6; DL 6) | "Preliminary operational matter", "not expected to be material" | No confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand assumed either way; preserve logs, investigate, require updates | Reject the materiality characterisation. Require investigation and updates. |
| **Sandbar renewals** (AUD 330,000) | "Ordinary-course operating costs" | Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction | Do not accept the characterisation. Assess the contracts. |
| **Title** | Evidenced by the share register at DD-012 | Independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence; DD-012 is an internal supplied source only | Reject. Require independent evidence. |
| **Tax / IP** | "Settled under the general regime" | Remain OPEN; no unlimited liability assumed; no resolution | Reject. Keep separate and open. |

## 2. Reasoning on the Material Issues

### A. Liability architecture: the package is a structural reduction, not a number change

The cap, thresholds, time limits and spillover clause work together, so their combined effect matters more than any single figure.

- **Thresholds.** Under the Seller's version, each claim must exceed AUD 25,000, and recovery starts only once aggregate claims exceed AUD 250,000, and then only for the excess. Consider AUD 300,000 of valid claims, each over AUD 25,000. Under our playbook (AUD 5,000 de minimis, AUD 50,000 tipping basket), the Seller is liable from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded, so we recover AUD 300,000. Under the Seller's version we recover AUD 50,000. The threshold change alone moves AUD 250,000 of exposure back to Wattlebridge.
- **Fundamental claims.** Subjecting title and capacity to the AUD 4.8m cap and 18-month window means a title defect could be capped and time-barred, which is the outcome the separate regime is designed to prevent.
- **Spillover and carve-outs.** "Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" and "applies to all Claims of any nature" would sweep fundamental and fraud claims into the general regime. The fraud carve-out needs to be express and non-waivable.

### B. Disclosure and buyer knowledge stack on each other

Disclosure paragraphs 1.1 and 1.2 deem disclosed everything in eleven data room documents, the Accounts, statutory registers and public records. Clause 8.3 then bars claims for anything the Buyer knew or could have discovered from those sources. Together, a buyer would be deemed to know the whole data room and public record and would have no claim for any of it. That is the structure the playbook rejects. We should also note that paragraph 1.1 covers DD-002 to DD-012 and does not mention DD-001. We should ask what DD-001 is and whether it is in the disclosure set.

### C. Completion conditions and funds flow

- **Bluefen.** DD-002 records about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue (roughly 30%) dependent on change-control consent. Disclosure paragraph 2 confirms that no final written consent or evidence of satisfied conditions is included. Consent-on-delivery and reasonable endeavours do not meet the playbook for a material customer consent. The condition should be effective consent and evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion.
- **Riverlark.** The approximately AUD 3.2m figure is an "approximately" figure as at 22 September, not a current payout. Disclosure paragraph 3 confirms the facility is unpaid and no discharge is in the data room. A post-completion release is exactly the outcome the playbook forbids without an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval. We should require a current payout letter and repayment from Completion funds, and treat the debt in the price mechanics consistent with our debt-free, cash-free baseline. We should also check that the security releases are effective (for example, PPSR discharge).
- **Bonuses.** Seller counsel says the AUD 420,000 is "a matter for the Seller" but the funds flow is silent on it. Disclosure paragraph 5 says the disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply. This is inconsistent: either the bonuses are a Seller cost, in which case they should be a specific line item or seller-funded, or they are Buyer cost, in which case the price must reflect them. Silence should not be accepted. The on-costs must be quantified.

### D. Specific risk items

- **Ironquay (cl 11.1).** The indemnity is confined to a SOW3 payment. Under DD-004 cl 7.3, transfer of SOW3 project materials depends on payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open, which is not independent bank verification either way. The Seller's indemnity does not address the IP transfer risk, and the cure (payment plus confirmatory assignment) should be preserved in any broadened indemnity. The AUD 180,000 should be verified through receipts or bank records before we rely on it.
- **DD-006 export incident.** About 1,240 records containing names, business emails, roles and activity timestamps may have been sent to an unintended external address. The Seller's "not expected to be material" is an opinion, not a finding. The investigation is preliminary, and the material does not establish access, scope or notification obligations. Our position should assume neither a confirmed breach nor a notification duty. We should require preservation of logs, an investigation with defined scope, and regular updates. Because personal information is involved, we recommend that privacy counsel assess whether any notification obligations could apply. We should not conclude either way. The team should also consider whether a specific indemnity is needed for this matter; that is my recommendation and not a playbook position.
- **Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000).** The three renewals are described as AUD 110,000 each in DD-008 and DD-011, and should be read together. The Seller's "ordinary-course" label is not a finding. The playbook requires assessment, not automatic Debt treatment or a price deduction. We should ask for the contract terms (whether each is unavoidable, terminable or accrued) and then decide whether any element is a pre-Completion liability for the price discussion.
- **Title.** The DD-012 register is an internal Seller document. Our playbook requires independent evidence: an ASIC company extract, transfer instruments, PPSR and encumbrance searches, and evidence of corporate authority and capacity.
- **Tax and IP.** Describing these as "settled under the general regime" is the kind of assertion the playbook says we should not accept. These remain open and must be kept separate from the general regime.
- **Other disclosed items.** Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009) are disclosed as notification or assignment matters, with the Seller saying they are not consent requirements. We should verify that conclusion against the underlying documents rather than accept the non-statement.

### E. Process and currency

- Amelia Frost's written approval is needed for the 20% cap, the 18-month period and the Riverlark post-completion release. None has been given, so these should not be signalled as acceptable in any communication.
- The disclosure is stated as at 5.00pm on 22 September 2026. Today is 6 November 2026. A bring-down of the disclosure and the data room is required before signing, and figures such as Riverlark, Ironquay and DD-006 should be refreshed.

## 3. Summary of Recommendations

1. **Reject the liability package as drafted.** Counter at 25% / AUD 6m cap, AUD 5,000 de minimis, AUD 50,000 tipping basket and 24-month general claims period. Do not offer the fallbacks without Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the draft.
2. **Ring-fence fundamental/title claims** with a 100% cap, at least six years, and outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. Include capacity.
3. **Delete the spillover language** ("any limitation applies to all Claims") and add an express, non-waivable fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance.
4. **Delete the general disclosure** of the data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public records (DL 1.1, 1.2, Sch 7). Require specific fair disclosure.
5. **Delete cl 8.3.** Any knowledge qualifier must name seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry, and must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
6. **Bluefen:** make effective consent plus evidence of cl 11.3 conditions a pre-Completion condition. Reject consent-on-delivery and reasonable endeavours.
7. **Riverlark:** obtain a current payout letter and repay directly from Completion funds, with effective security releases. Reject post-completion release unless there is an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval.
8. **Employee bonuses:** itemise the AUD 420,000 and the triggered on-costs in the funds flow as either a deduction or Seller-funded.
9. **Ironquay:** broaden the indemnity, preserve the SOW3 cure (payment plus confirmatory assignment), and verify the AUD 180,000 through bank or receipt evidence.
10. **DD-006:** require log preservation, a scoped investigation and regular updates. Obtain privacy advice on notification obligations. Do not assume a breach, harm or demand, and consider a specific indemnity.
11. **Sandbar:** obtain the renewal terms and assess them. Do not apply automatic Debt treatment or a price deduction.
12. **Title:** require independent title, encumbrance and authority evidence. DD-012 alone is insufficient.
13. **Tax and IP:** keep open and separate from the general regime. Reject "settled" language.
14. **Process:** request a bring-down of the disclosure and data room, refresh stale figures, confirm DD-001, and verify the DD-007 and DD-009 conclusions.

These are commercial and drafting positions drawn from our playbook. The NSW governing law points, the privacy analysis and the enforceability of the fraud carve-out should be confirmed by responsible counsel before we send the mark-up.
